endorsements.quote: Minimum evaluation: Multi-site external validation across at least three geographically and device-diverse centers; report GRR and per-subgroup performance with confidence intervals.
The observational experiments for human-AI interaction trials should be applied that endoscopists use model outputs in a simulated or live environment to measure behavioral changes.
The DL-based segmentation models’ performance should also be evaluated by stratification of patient subgroups, scope equipment, and operator experience.

Develop and enforce standardized annotation protocol and labeling guidelines; multi-expert consensus labeling; adjudication workflows; active learning to prioritize ambiguous cases; periodic re-annotation audits

Minimum evaluation: Observational human-AI interaction studies in simulated or live settings measuring decision change, task time, false positive-driven unnecessary interventions, and clinician trust/usability in accordance to standardized scales.
The prospective and multi-institutional testing should be included in regulatory-grade validation with pre-specified performance thresholds and prespecified failure modes.

unlisted_practices: Adopt sensitivity-weighted and lesion-level outcome metrics with per-class clinical-risk curves rather than relying on mean IoU alone.
Realign funding and publication incentives to reward clinical validation and replication over leaderboard performance.
Build shared annotation infrastructure and consenting frameworks for multi-center data.
Evaluate cost-effectiveness, including computational costs and annotation burden, of AI tools before adoption.
Evaluate the computational efficiency, latency, and memory footprint of AI models on intended clinical hardware.
Use federated learning and multi-center data sharing to improve dataset diversity.

screen.reason: Editorial commentary discussing a comparative deep learning segmentation study and proposing a framework/agenda for safe and clinically-minded deployment in endoscopy.
